drugs/androgens/dht-derivatives/primobol.title: Primobolan
drugs/androgens/dht-derivatives/primobol.content: Methenolone or brand name Primobolan, an anabolic androgenic steroid, derived from dihydrotestosterone (DHT). It comes as an oral tablet (methenolone acetate) or an injection (methenolone enanthate, often called Primobolan Depot). It was originally used medically to treat muscle wasting and anemia, but it is now largely discontinued for official medical use.

drugs/androgens/testosterone-derivatives.title: Testosterone propionate
drugs/androgens/testosterone-derivatives.content:
About

Testosterone propionate is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid medication. It features a short ester chain that makes it a fast-acting, short-release form of testosterone. It is historically used to treat low testosterone levels in men (hypogonadism)and certain types of breast cancer in women via IM injections.
Mechanism of Action

Direct
Skeletal Muscle
T acts directly on skeletal muscle through the androgen receptor (AR), promoting an anabolic state and supporting muscle protein synthesis and hypertrophy. T is Associated with increased IGF-1 expression and activation of PI3K Akt and mTORC1. Akt-mediated phosphorylation of FoxO transcription factors suppresses the expression of atrophy related ubiquitin ligases such as MuRF1 and atrogin-1/MAFbx, thus reducing activation of the ubiquitin–proteasome proteolytic system. Testosterone can also stimulate ERK and mTOR signaling directly in muscle cells, contributing to hypertrophic growth.
Osteoprogenitors
Osteoprogenitors / early osteoblasts T acts directly via AR, promoting proliferation and osteogenic maturation. Testosterone → AR → genomic transcription → ↑ ALP/TNSALP → matrix maturation/mineralization, with testosterone itself also shown to stimulate osteoblast proliferation. More specific kinase pathways remain less established for testosterone than DHT.
Osteoblasts
Promoting proliferation and osteoblasts activity via AR activity. Testosterone → AR → genomic signaling → ↑ ALP/TNSALP and osteocalcin → matrix maturation/mineralization, while increased TGF-β signaling may further contribute to proliferation.
Osteocytes
T acts directly on osteocytes through AR, with AR expression increasing during osteocyte differentiation. Testosterone-AR signalling contributes to osteocyte-mediated regulation of bone remodelling and potential interactions of mechanotransduction downstream pathways such as SOST, RANKL and OPG. However, unlike osteoblasts and osteoprogenitors, the specific downstream mechanisms of testosterone signalling in osteocytes remain less well established. Evidence supports an important role for osteocyte AR in maintaining trabecular bone, theses specific pathways are less established.
Rental / Erythropoiesis
T stimulates erythropoiesis through renal, iron and potentially direct haematopoietic mechanisms. Testosterone → AR → ↑ EPO production in the kidney → EPOR/JAK2/STAT5 signalling in erythroid progenitors → ↑ erythroid survival and proliferation. T also suppresses hepatic hepcidin through BMP/SMAD signalling → ↑ ferroportin activity and iron availability → increased haemoglobin synthesis and erythropoiesis via AR activation.
Water / Sodium Retention
Testosterone can act directly on the renal tubule through AR signalling to increase ENaC expression. T → AR → ↑ αENaC transcription, with evidence for direct androgen-responsive regulation of the αENaC promoter; testosterone also increases α, β and γ ENaC expression in the distal nephron/collecting duct in animal models. Testosterone may also enhance renal Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity associated with increased Na⁺ transport, although direct AR activation is limited.
Indirect
Aromatization
T → CYP19A1 → 17β-estradiol (E2)
5-alpha reductase
T → 5-Alpha Reductase type 1/2 → DHT

drugs/diuretics/potassium-sparring-diure.title: Amiloride
drugs/diuretics/potassium-sparring-diure.content:
About

Amiloride is a mild potassium-sparing diuretic medication used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, and fluid retention (edema). It helps the body get rid of extra water and salt while preventing potassium loss.
Mechanism of Action

Direct
ENaC
Amiloride directly inhibits the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the late distal convoluted tubule, connecting tubule and collecting duct, reducing Na⁺ reabsorption and producing mild natriuresis. This mechanism is independent of aldosterone signalling, as amiloride blocks the channel directly regardless of circulating aldosterone levels.
Indirect
Potassium Sparing
ENaC blockade reduces the lumen-negative transepithelial potential generated by Na⁺ reabsorption. This decreases secretion of K⁺ via ROMK and H⁺ by intercalated cells, producing potassium retention and a tendency toward metabolic acidosis. Magnesium excretion may also be modestly reduced.
RAAS
Mild extracellular-volume contraction activates RAAS and increases aldosterone secretion. However, because ENaC is pharmacologically blocked, aldosterone cannot fully stimulate distal Na⁺ reabsorption, blunting the kidney’s response to this compensatory hormonal signal.
Uric Acid
Amiloride has little effect on uric-acid handling compared with thiazide or loop diuretics. Any reduction in urate excretion is generally mild and secondary to volume contraction rather than a direct effect on urate transport.
Pure Off Target
NHEs (particularly NHE1)
Amiloride inhibits Na⁺/H⁺ exchangers, particularly NHE1, and was the original pharmacological tool used to characterize NHE activity before development of more selective inhibitors such as EIPA and cariporide.
ASICs
At higher concentrations, amiloride blocks acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs), making it the classic experimental inhibitor of ASIC currents. This action is unrelated to its renal diuretic effects.
Na⁺/Ca²⁺ Exchanger (NCX)
Amiloride inhibits the Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchanger at higher micromolar concentrations, contributing to experimental cardiac and vascular effects independent of ENaC.
uPA
Amiloride directly and competitively inhibits urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA) by binding within its catalytic S1 specificity pocket. This off-target action has been studied in nephrotic syndrome and cancer biology because it reduces plasmin generation and downstream proteolytic signalling.

drugs/diuretics/thiazide-diuretics/hydro.title: Hydrochlorothiazide
drugs/diuretics/thiazide-diuretics/hydro.content:
About

Hydrochlorothiazide moderate prescription thiazide diuretic, It is primarily used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and to reduce fluid retention (edema). associated with conditions like congestive heart failure, liver cirrhosis, and kidney disorders.
Mechanism of Action

Direct
NCC
HCTZ directly inhibits the Na⁺/Cl⁻ cotransporter (NCC/SLC12A3) in the distal convoluted tubule → ↓ NaCl reabsorption → ↑ Na⁺ and Cl⁻ excretion → natriuresis and diuresis. Reduced extracellular fluid volume produces the initial fall in blood pressure, while chronic treatment produces a sustained reduction in peripheral vascular resistance.
Indirect
Hypokalaemia
↑ Distal Na⁺ delivery + RAAS/aldosterone activation → ↑ ENaC-mediated Na⁺ reabsorption → more negative tubular lumen → ↑ K⁺ secretion through ROMK → hypokalaemia and metabolic alkalosis.
Hypocalciuria / Hypercalcaemia
NCC inhibition → ↓ intracellular Na⁺ in DCT cells → ↑ basolateral NCX1 activity → ↓ intracellular Ca²⁺ → ↑ TRPV5-mediated apical Ca²⁺ entry → ↑ distal Ca²⁺ reabsorption → ↓ urinary Ca²⁺. This contributes to thiazide prevention of calcium-containing kidney stones and may have a bone-sparing effect.
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
Mild ECF contraction → ↑ proximal Na⁺ and water reabsorption → ↓ distal tubular delivery → ↓ urine volume, thereby reducing polyuria despite HCTZ being a diuretic.
Glucose intolerance / diabetes
HCTZ-induced hypokalaemia may impair insulin secretion, although this mechanism is not fully established. More recent experimental evidence identifies mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase 5b (CA5b) in pancreatic β-cells as a thiazide target: CA5b inhibition → ↓ mitochondrial HCO₃⁻ availability → ↓ anaplerotic oxaloacetate production → impaired metabolic signalling and insulin secretion. This mechanism is strongly supported experimentally but currently rests predominantly on animal/islet data rather than definitive human evidence.
Hyperuricaemia / gout
HCTZ alters proximal-tubular urate handling → ↓ renal uric-acid excretion → ↑ serum urate → increased risk of hyperuricaemia and gout.
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition
Thiazides retain carbonic-anhydrase inhibitory activity, but CA inhibition is not the principal mechanism responsible for HCTZ’s therapeutic natriuresis; NCC inhibition is the dominant pharmacological target.
Vascular effects
Chronic thiazide therapy produces sustained vasodilation/reduced peripheral resistance, but the precise molecular mechanism remains incompletely defined. Experimental effects involving vascular ion channels, carbonic anhydrase and prostaglandins have been proposed, but they should not be presented as established primary mechanisms.

drugs/diuretics/thiazide-diuretics/index.title: Thiazide diuretics
drugs/diuretics/thiazide-diuretics/index.content:
About

Thiazide diuretics are prescription water pills like Hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, and indapamide used primarily to treat high blood pressure and fluid swelling.
Mechanism of Action

Blocking salt and water reabsorption in the early part of the kidney’s distal convoluted tubule, lower total fluid volume in the body to reduce heart strain, and open up blood vessels over time to keep blood pressure down.
Molecular Structure



Composition: true thiazide-type, benzothiadiazine ring: HCTZ, Chlorothiazide
Composition: thiazide-like, lacking classic benzothiadiazine ring system: Chlorthalidone, Indapamide
Common Use Cases

Hypertension
Mild fluid build-up or swelling from heart failure
Lowering calcium levels in urine to prevent certain kidney stones.

drugs/hair-agents/5-alpha-reductase-inhi.title: Dutasteride
drugs/hair-agents/5-alpha-reductase-inhi.content:
About

Dutasteride is a potent, off-label oral and topical medication used to treat pattern hair loss (Androgenetic alopecia). It works by blocking type 1 and type 2 5-alpha-reductase enzymes, reducing DHT.

drugs/hair-agents/5-alpha-reductase-inhi.title: Finasteride
drugs/hair-agents/5-alpha-reductase-inhi.content:
About

Finasteride is a prescription oral tablet used to treat male pattern hair loss (Androgenetic alopecia) by lowering scalp hormone levels. It works by inhibiting the 5-alpha-reductase enzyme, preventing testosterone from converting into DHT.

drugs/hair-agents/anti-androgens/ru-5884.title: RU-58841
drugs/hair-agents/anti-androgens/ru-5884.content:
About

RU-58841 is an experimental, non-steroidal antiandrogen compound developed to treat hair loss and acne, functioning as a topical DHT blocker. Off-label for Androgenetic alopecia, but it lacks regulatory approval, large-scale human clinical safety data.

drugs/osteoanabolic-agents/abaloparatide.title: Abaloparatide
drugs/osteoanabolic-agents/abaloparatide.content:
About

Abaloparatide is an anabolic, bone-building prescription medicine used to treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk for fractures. It’s a 34-amino acid peptide analog of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP), (brand names like Tymlos and Eladynos), and administered daily subq.
Mechanism of Action

Direct
Direct
PTH1R
Abaloparatide is a synthetic PTHrP(1–34) analogue and selective PTH1R agonist. It preferentially binds the RG, G-protein-coupled conformation of PTH1R, producing a relatively transient Gs → adenylyl cyclase → cAMP → PKA signal. Abaloparatide can also engage additional PTH1R pathways, including PLC/Ca²⁺ and β-arrestin signalling, but Gs/cAMP/PKA is the principal pathway associated with its osteoanabolic action.
SOST
PTH1R → Gs → cAMP → PKA → ↓ SIK2/3 activity → HDAC4/5 nuclear translocation → ↓ MEF2-dependent SOST transcription → ↓ sclerostin. This removes inhibition of Wnt signalling and promotes osteoblast activity.
Wnt/β-catenin
↓ Sclerostin → increased availability of LRP5/6 → ↑ Wnt/β-catenin signalling → increased osteoblast differentiation/activity and bone formation.
RANKL/OPG
PTH1R signalling regulates osteoblast RANKL expression through cAMP/PKA-dependent pathways involving SIK2/3 and CRTC proteins. Abaloparatide produces a more favourable RANKL/OPG balance than prolonged PTH1R stimulation, contributing to a greater formation-over-resorption effect.
Indirect
IHH–PTHrP
PTHrP → PTH1R → PKA → maintenance of proliferative chondrocyte phenotype → delayed hypertrophic differentiation → delayed endochondral ossification.

drugs/osteoanabolic-agents/odanacatib.title: Odanacatib
drugs/osteoanabolic-agents/odanacatib.content:
About

Odanacatib is an investigational oral medication that was developed to treat postmenopausal osteoporosis by blocking cathepsin K, an enzyme that breaks down bone tissue. Although it proved effective at increasing bone density, its development was discontinued.
Mechanism of Action

Direct
Cathepsin K Inhibition
Odanacatib is a selective, potent and reversible inhibitor of cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts. Cathepsin K acts as the major collagenase responsible for degradation of type I collagen in the organic bone matrix during bone remodelling. Odanacatib → binds to and inhibits CatK in osteoclasts → osteoclasts cannot degrade demineralized collagen in the resorption lacunae → ↓ bone resorption. Unlike bisphosphonates or denosumab, odanacatib does not affect osteoclastogenesis or osteoclast survival.
Indirect
Maintained osteoclast viability / Rebound resorption
ODN preserves osteoclast numbers (supported by sustained or ↑ TRAP5b). Upon withdrawal → abrupt restoration of CatK activity → rapid ↑ in short collagen resorption markers (sNTx, uNTx) → rebound bone loss and potential ↑ fracture risk during drug withdrawal.
Uncoupled bone remodelling / ↑ BMD
↓ short/medium resorption markers (sNTx, uNTx) but only transient ↓ in sCTx, with accumulation of larger partially degraded fragments (sICTP). Bone formation markers (sPINP, sBSAP) show minimal early suppression and return near baseline over time → uncoupled remodelling (resorption ↓, formation relatively maintained) → net positive bone balance → progressive ↑ in lumbar spine and hip BMD.
Off-target cerebrovascular risk
Off-target effects (mechanism incompletely defined; may involve CatK expression in vascular smooth muscle or off-target inhibition of other cathepsins) → ↑ incidence of cerebrovascular events (stroke) in the LOFT trial → primary reason for regulatory withdrawal, despite robust antifracture efficacy.

drugs/osteoanabolic-agents/vosoritide.content:
About

Vosoritide (sold under the brand name Voxzogo) is a prescription medication used to increase linear growth in children with achondroplasia (the most common form of dwarfism) who have open growth plates.

hormones/steroid-hormones/dht.title: DHT
hormones/steroid-hormones/dht.content:
About

DHT stands for dihydrotestosterone. It is a strong male sex hormone made from testosterone with the help of an enzyme. DHT helps build male sex traits during early growth and puberty. It can also shrink hair follicles and lead to hair loss

hormones/steroid-hormones/e2.title: E2
hormones/steroid-hormones/e2.content:
About

E2 also know as 17-beta-estradiol, , is the primary and most potent estradiol (estrogen) sex hormone produced in the human body. It plays a crucial role in regulating reproductive cycles, bone density, cardiovascular health, and other metabolic functions in both females and males.

hormones/steroid-hormones/testosterone.title: testosterone

More specific kinase pathways remain less established for testosterone than DHT.

Evidence supports an important role for osteocyte AR in maintaining trabecular bone, theses specific pathways are less established.

Testosterone → AR → ↑ EPO production in the kidney → EPOR/JAK2/STAT5 signalling in erythroid progenitors → ↑ erythroid survival and proliferation. pathways/mtorc1.title: mTORC1
pathways/mtorc1.content:
About

The mTOR aslo know as mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, it’s pathway is a core cellular network that senses nutrients, energy, and growth factors to regulate cell growth, protein synthesis, and metabolism. Acting as a master switch, it balances building up tissues (anabolism) with cellular cleanup and repair (catabolism/autophagy).

repectors/ar.title: AR
repectors/ar.content:
About

The androgen receptor (AR) is a nuclear receptor protein activated by male sex hormones like testosterone and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). It acts as a transcription factor to control gene activity, driving male sexual development, muscle growth, bone density, and specific disease states like prostate cancer.

transporters/channels/enac.title: ENaC
transporters/channels/enac.content:
About

ENaC stands for the epithelial sodium channel, a special protein pore in cell walls that lets pass Na⁺ through. It is found mainly in the kidneys, lungs, and colon, where it helps control salt and water levels in the body.
Mechanism

Activation
Hormones: Aldosterone, vasopressin
Protease Enzymes: Proteolytic Cleavage furin, prostasin, plasmin
Mechanical Stress: Fluid movement, physical forces over cells
Apical Entry
ENaC lets Na⁺ ions flow passively down their combined electrochemical gradient from the extracellular fluid or lumen into the epithelial cell. The inside of the cell has a negative electrical potential relative to the lumen, which actively pulls the positively charged sodium ions inward.
Basolateral Removal
The Na+/K+-ATPase pumps the entered Na⁺ out across the basolateral membrane into the blood, using energy to maintain low intracellular sodium levels.
Coupled Transport
The inward movement of sodium via ENaC creates an osmotic and electrical environment that secondary transporters and water reabsorption rely upon.

Molecular Structure

Composition: Heterotrimer, α, β, and γ subunits
